extract() doesn't know about cleaning rules; load() doesn't know where the data came from. That separation is the whole point.

code:
def run_pipeline(source_path, target_path):
    raw_df = extract(source_path)
    clean_df = transform(raw_df)
    rows_loaded = load(clean_df, target_path)
    print(f"Loaded {rows_loaded} rows (from {len(raw_df)} extracted).")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_pipeline("orders.csv", "orders_clean.csv")
caption: Its only job is to call the three stages in order and pass each output to the next — no cleaning logic lives here.

subtitle: A real pipeline rarely has just one source.
